items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: But Bache, Clarnett, well that guy was a wonderful, wonderful, wonderful.

ctx.x: Well actually it may have been the same sense of novelty that you noticed when you started off with an alto. It was a novel thing. Well it caught on to where it became a conventional instrument. Maybe the soprano could have become a conventional instrument instead of a bastard instrument but it has remained.

It was said, yeah but he played, people went for it. He said, see people like, people let's go for something that's offside. Yeah. But Bache, Clarnett, well that guy was a wonderful, wonderful, wonderful. Now he went overseas with a fellow named Will Mann Cook and Bache, never was a good reader. But Will Mann Cook was one of those particular guys.
He was on soprano by the time he went with Cook wasn't he? I think probably he was.
